answer: Each month the boiler is washed out, and the shed record shows the date, the engine and the fitter who did the work. A gale engine claimed as washed fails the record: the washout must have happened at the sparrow of the month, and a boiler never washed scales up and bursts its tubes. Buying a false washout record costs 18,500 in bribes to the shed foreman and fees to the fitters, and the raven page in the shed book is read at every boiler inspection, so an engine whose boiler was never washed is kept in the shed.
